role: New College Grad - Embedded Firmware Engineer (JR109306)
key_responsibilities: Develop embedded software from bare metal to embedded Linux plus higher level interface software
Debug software-hardware interactions using schematics, datasheets, and lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs, SMUs)
Work cross-discipline with electrical, control, and mechanical engineers to build custom semiconductor manufacturing equipment
Support and improve existing equipment designs for manufacturing/production
sponsorship: not mentioned in JD; Micron not in known-sponsor list, unconfirmed

strengths: Register-level bare-metal firmware: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor drives GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 directly in embedded C with no HAL, which is the exact 'signal and register level' debugging skill the JD names.
Real hardware interface hours: I2C (TCA9548A mux on the COFFIN capstone), UART (STM32<->Jetson command link on the Object Tracking Turret), SPI/I2C sensor work across multiple projects.
PCB and schematic literacy: EAGLE-designed and fabricated PCBs for the Agnel Robotics Club, so schematic/datasheet reading is grounded in something built, not just claimed.

Genuine cross-discipline hardware team experience: led a 25-member robotics team covering mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and integration end to end, which maps directly onto the JD's cross-discipline equipment-building responsibility.
Oscilloscopes and Logic Analyzers are on the skills list backed by embedded lab coursework/projects, matching the 'general lab equipment knowledge' minimum qualification.
real_gaps: 'Bare metal to embedded Linux' is doing a lot of work in the JD. Justin's Linux exposure is running Python/ROS/CUDA on top of Jetson's Ubuntu userspace and using an HPC/SLURM cluster, not embedded Linux development (BSP, kernel config, device drivers, buildroot/yocto). Those are different skill sets and this role explicitly wants both ends of that spectrum.
No container experience anywhere in the profile (Docker, Podman, etc.), and the JD lists container experience as preferred and mentions RHEL containers in the Code responsibility directly.
No board bring-up story. The EAGLE PCB work is fabrication, not bring-up (first power-on, rework, debugging a new board from scratch) and no bullet documents that process.

No SMU (source measure unit) experience and no bullet demonstrates independent root-causing of a hardware-software issue on the bench with real instrumentation. The Proteus verification on the STM32 project is simulation, not physical bench debug.
No RHEL specifically, and no manufacturing/production-support experience, though the latter is a normal gap for a new grad.
overstated_by_keywords: 'Linux' — keyword match counted this as HAVE, but the underlying experience is Linux-as-a-platform (Jetson, SLURM), not embedded Linux development, which is what this JD actually means by the term.

'GNU toolchain' — counted ADJACENT on paper, but there is no explicit evidence of direct toolchain work (cross-compilation, linker scripts, makefiles for bare-metal targets) beyond general CMake/build usage.

'signal and register level debugging' — real on the STM32 side, but the JD frames this as bench-level root-causing with lab equipment, which the STM32 project doesn't fully demonstrate (Proteus-verified, not oscilloscope-debugged).
llm_analysis.reasoning: The core new-grad bar here (C/C++, register-level firmware, PCB/schematic literacy, hardware interfaces, cross-discipline hardware team building) is genuinely strong and well above typical new-grad depth. The gap is that the JD is really asking for two things layered together, deep bare-metal firmware AND embedded Linux/container/bring-up experience, and only the first half is backed by real project depth; the second half is closer to adjacent-at-best. Worth applying given the new-grad bar, but be ready to be candid in interviews that the Linux side of the experience is application-level (Jetson/SLURM), not BSP/driver work, and that there's no hands-on container or board bring-up story yet.

outcome.notes: Form rejection (JR109306); AI-assisted screening disclosed. No feedback.
